subject: setting prior for a covariate with missing value depending on a categorical covariate

messages.subject: setting prior for a covariate with missing value depending on a categorical covariate
parts:
Hello everyone,

I'm new to jags and trying to write my code in R. There are some missing data in my covariate x and I'd like to set prior for these missing values based on a categorical covariate (called prior.x) with 4 community choices. So, I created indicator variables (community_1, ..., community_4) to indicate the community of individual i belongs to and set prior accordingly. However, I received the error message below when compiling. I also tried to code it up like the one shown in # below instead but that doesn't seem to help and still get the same error message. 

Any suggestions would be greatly received!

Thanks!
Grace


cat("model

{

for (i in 1:N){

y[i] ~ dnorm(y.hat[i], tau)

y.hat[i]<-a + b * x[i]

}

## model for missing x

for (i in 1:N){

x[i] ~ dnorm(mu.x[i], prec.x)


# mu.x[i] ~ r[1] + r[2] * ifelse(prior.x[i]=='community1', 1, 0) + r[3] * ifelse(prior.x[i]=='community2', 1, 0) + r[4] * ifelse(prior.x[i]=='community3', 1, 0) + r[5] * ifelse(prior.x[i]=='community4', 1, 0)

community_1[i]<-ifelse(prior.x[i]=='community1', 1, 0)

community_2[i]<-ifelse(prior.x[i]=='community2', 1, 0)

community_3[i]<-ifelse(prior.x[i]=='community3', 1, 0)

community_4[i]<-ifelse(prior.x[i]=='community4', 1, 0)

mu.x[i] ~ r[1] + r[2] * community_1[i] + r[3] * community_2[i] + r[4] * community_3[i] + r[5] * community_4[i]


}

a ~ dnorm(0, .0001)

b ~ dnorm(0, .0001)

prec.x ~ dgamma(.01, .01)

tau <- pow(sigma, -2)

sigma ~ dunif(0, 100)

for (k in 1:5){

r[k] ~ dnorm(0.0, .001)

}

}", file="model2.txt")

# compile the model

jags.model2<-jags.model(file="model2.txt", data=list("N"=10000, "y"=mydata$y, "x"=mydata$x, "prior.x"=mydata$cummunity), n.chains=1, n.adapt=500)

messages.subject: Re: setting prior for a covariate with missing value depending on a categorical covariate
parts:
Hi Grace,

I think you were close to what you wanted, but I have suggested a different method below in a (hopefully) helpful manner. I am no expert myself, but I hope this points you in the right direction. I also suggest if you have future questions about JAGS (rather than NIMBLE) that you may wish to ask them on a more JAGS specific group, such as hmecology or the JAGS discussion page. 


I would try a nested indexing approach to solve this problem, rather than ifelse statements within JAGS. If I were writing this model, I might do:

model

     {

    for (i in 1:N){

       y[i] ~ dnorm(y.hat[i], tau)

       y.hat[i]<-a + b * x[i]

    }

 ## model for missing x

   
    for (i in 1:N){
x[i] ~ dnorm(mu.x[i], prec.x)
mu.x[i] <- r[1] + r[prior.x[i]] #nested indexing

}

             

      a ~ dnorm(0, .0001)

     b ~ dnorm(0, .0001)

     prec.x ~ dgamma(.01, .01)      

      tau <- pow(sigma, -2)

     sigma ~ dunif(0, 100)

     

     for (k in 1:5){

         r[k] ~ dnorm(0.0, .001)

        }
   

  }

And then when you pass the data to jags:

prior.x = mydata$community+1 #where mydata$community is numbers between 1 and 4, 1 = community 1, 2 = community 2, etc.  
jags.model2<-jags.model(file="model2.txt", data=list(N = 10000, y = mydata$y, x = mydata$x, prior.x = prior.x), n.chains = 1, n.adapt=500)


So for instance, if the 4th x were missing, but you knew it was from community 2, mu.x[i] would be r[1] + r[2]. Note that if prior.x is anything outside of 1:5, JAGS will throw an error since you only defined r[1] through r[5]. 

As a side note, the "~" is only for distributions, so you'll want to use the "<-" if you're assigning a value to mu.x[i] (as you are in this case). 

Hope that helps!
